title: Zenith Accelerators — integration discovery & pilot scoping
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack (SOC2 + network diagram) and onboarding checklist
Zenith to provide access window for on-site benchmark (week of 2026-04-20)
Schedule technical deep-dive with Zenith infra team (Lucas + Ravi) - target 2026-04-18
action_items: Lucas Nguyen: prepare benchmark script + docker image for Zenith A100 cluster - Due 2026-04-18
Maya Patel: send partner commercial starter packet and draft pilot pricing - Due 2026-04-14
Olivia Hart: gather PCI/PHI use-cases and any compliance questions to send to Redwood - Due 2026-04-15
summary: Introductory discovery for potential integration partnership. Discussed deployment modes (hosted vs private), pilot goals, security/compliance needs, initial perf targets, and next steps for benchmark and commercial proposals.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood Inference. Lucas is our solutions engineer, he'll cover the technical bits. Olivia, Ravi, Samira, thanks for taking the time.

[00:12] Olivia Hart: Hi Maya, hi Lucas, good to meet you all. Excited to talk through the potential integrator work between Zenith and Redwood.

[00:20] Lucas Nguyen: Hi folks. Quick agenda from our side: 1) understand Zenith's product + infra, 2) what a pilot looks like, 3) security/compliance questions, and 4) timing + next steps. Sound OK?

[00:32] Ravi Singh: Yep that works. For context, Zenith Accelerators builds rack-level GPU acceleration appliances; we sell to telco and cloud service providers. Most of our customers want a turnkey model with an inference runtime on top.

[00:45] Samira Lopez: And we're exploring partners who can provide a production-grade inference stack we can bundle, ideally with low-latency routing and some of the Redwood tooling features — cost controls, rollouts.

[01:05] Maya Patel: Great. Can you share current stack? Are you running Kubernetes on-prem, bare metal, or something else?

[01:12] Ravi Singh: Mostly on-prem racks with a mix — customers run either our lightweight k8s distro or raw systemd-managed containers. Typical hardware is 4–8x A100 per node, NVMe local, NFS for model artifacts.

[01:28] Lucas Nguyen: Ok that's helpful. The main integration approaches we see: 1) Redwood Private — deploy our control plane in your VPC/on-prem and run inference runtime on your GPUs, 2) Dedicated — reserved pools we host for you in cloud regions, or 3) a hybrid where models are served on-prem but routing and observability is in the Redwood managed control plane.

[01:50] Olivia Hart: We prefer a Partner-Embedded workflow where Zenith can resell a managed inference offering. So Private + some console-level multi-tenant controls would be ideal.

[02:05] Maya Patel: Understood. From a pilot perspective we typically do a short integration: a 2–4 week on-site benchmark plus a 6–8 week pilot for a small set of customers. What's your internal timeline?

[02:20] Olivia Hart: We want to go to market with a joint offering in Q3, so a May pilot start would be perfect.

[02:30] Lucas Nguyen: Sounds feasible. For benchmarking, we'll need SSH access to a test rack or a VPN with a test tenant. We prefer to run our KV cache and batching tests, and measure latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, and memory/KV hit rates.

[02:49] Ravi Singh: We can provide a dev rack next week for 48 hours. One note — our infra team is strict about inbound access windows and we use a private jump host, so we'll share the access SOP.

[03:02] Maya Patel: Perfect. On security, what are the main compliance ask? SOC 2? Data residency? KMS integration?

[03:12] Samira Lopez: Many of our customers ask for SOC 2 and sometimes FIPS-aligned key storage. They also ask about audit logs — who did what, when.

[03:22] Lucas Nguyen: We can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping and provide detailed audit logs. We'll send our SOC 2 + network diagram. Note: some transcription got our KMS as 'kay-em-ess' lol — just flagging.

[03:35] Olivia Hart: Ha, good to know. Also, for the private offering we need RBAC and SSO — support for SAML or OIDC.

[03:45] Maya Patel: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SSO provisioning, and role-based access controls at route/model/token granularity. We'll include the RBAC model doc in the materials.

[03:56] Ravi Singh: Great. On the runtime side, two technical constraints: 1) some customers keep models in an internal artifact registry with signed images, and 2) they need deterministic model pinning for compliance. How does Redwood handle model variant pinning?

[04:10] Lucas Nguyen: We expose model version pins and immutable artifacts. For on-prem we'll allow your registry endpoints and we can verify signatures. We also support quantized variants and automatic fallback to lower-precision models when memory or latency constraints force a tradeoff.

[04:28] Samira Lopez: Fallback behavior is interesting — customers worry about quality regressions when going from FP16 to INT8. Do you have quality-monitoring?

[04:36] Lucas Nguyen: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring against prompt sets and can alert on regressions, plus A/B rollout controls. For pilots we recommend establishing an acceptance prompt set so we can track delta in generation quality.

[04:52] Olivia Hart: Re: pricing — are you flexible for partner resale? We want margin to bundle support.

[04:58] Maya Patel: We have partner pricing tiers for Dedicated and Private. For pilots we typically provide a starter commercial that includes discounted reserved capacity pricing and integration hours. I'll follow up with a partner commercial packet.

[05:12] Ravi Singh: Back to technical — can Redwood's runtime run without a full k8s control plane? Some of our customers prefer systemd or our minimal orchestrator because they want predictable latency and less overhead.

[05:25] Lucas Nguyen: Yes, our runtime can be packaged as a container or a binary and run under systemd or your lightweight orchestrator. The main requirement is a process supervisor and access to NVMe and GPU devices; we handle kernel selection and batching inside the runtime.

[05:44] Maya Patel: Also want to surface typical performance numbers for similar setups so Zenith can set expectations with customers. Lucas, could you share an example?

[05:52] Lucas Nguyen: Sure — rough numbers: on a 4xA100 node with 32k context, continuous batching, we see about 120–180 tokens/sec for a Llama-70B-type model with KV caching enabled, P95 latency around 70–150ms depending on prompt distribution. Those numbers vary a lot with quantization and kernel sets.

[06:18] Olivia Hart: That's useful. Our sales team wants low-latency claims; we need tight SLAs. How does Redwood handle graceful degradation if a rack is overloaded?

[06:28] Lucas Nguyen: We have smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants or cross-rack failover. For partner deployments we can configure admission control and per-tenant quotas to protect latency SLOs.

[06:44] Ravi Singh: On the network side, what are the port requirements? Our SOC team will want a list for the firewall.

[06:52] Maya Patel: We'll include a minimal network diagram and port list. Typically we need outbound to the control plane for telemetry and a few inbound ports if you host the control plane. We can use an agent if you prefer outbound-only.

[07:05] Samira Lopez: Would prefer outbound-only for many customers. Inbound opens up too many audit controls.

[07:11] Lucas Nguyen: Outbound-only telemetry with a reverse tunnel or agent is supported; it just changes how we orchestrate model rollouts.

[07:21] Olivia Hart: Let's talk pilot acceptance criteria. We suggest: 1) P50 latency under 50ms for short prompts on target models, 2) throughput to support N concurrent sessions (we'll define exact numbers), and 3) no data exfil risk and audit logs present.

[07:36] Maya Patel: That looks good. We usually add cost per token metrics so customers can model unit economics. Lucas can run a cost sensitivity test during benchmarking.

[07:45] Lucas Nguyen: Yep I'll run token-cost sensitivity and show how batching and KV cache affect unit cost.

[07:52] Ravi Singh: For the benchmark, which models do you want us to host versus you host? Some customers want to keep models entirely internal.

[08:00] Lucas Nguyen: We can do either. For the pilot it's easiest to test with a Redwood-provisioned model image pulled into your private registry; if customers require complete separation, we can run everything inside your network.

[08:15] Olivia Hart: One more compliance item — we occasionally see customers asking for a separate control-plane for auditability. Does Redwood support isolated control planes per tenant?

[08:24] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Private can be instantiated as a separate control plane per tenant or a multi-tenant control plane with per-tenant isolation. We'll share options and tradeoffs.

[08:36] Samira Lopez: Good. Also curious about support SLAs — who handles second-line support for the runtime when it's embedded in Zenith's bundle?

[08:45] Maya Patel: For partner embeds we offer co-support models: Zenith handles L1 onboarding and we provide L2/L3 support with escalations. We can draft an SLO map in the partner agreement.

[08:58] Ravi Singh: That helps. Now a couple of deep tech questions — are there known kernel/channel optimizations for Ampere vs Hopper we should be aware of? We've seen kernel differences change perf by 20%.

[09:12] Lucas Nguyen: We have a kernel selector in the runtime that picks kernels based on hardware and sequence length distributions. We also maintain a compatibility matrix — Hopper tends to be better for large context lengths with certain attention ops, but Ampere/NVidia Ampere configs are highly performant for medium contexts. We'll share matrix notes; some of those got garbled in notes as 'hipper' or similar.

[09:36] Olivia Hart: Haha. Any gotchas around driver versions or CUDA mismatches?

[09:41] Lucas Nguyen: Yes, driver and libc versions matter. We'll provide a validated list of driver + CUDA + cuDNN combos. For on-prem customers we recommend using our validated image to avoid subtle perf regressions.

[09:58] Maya Patel: Funding/commercial question — do you have budget set aside to pay for a pilot or should we expect Zenith to front integration hours?

[10:06] Olivia Hart: We have a small partner enablement budget. We can cover integration hours for proof-of-concept work but would lean on a co-funded pilot if possible.

[10:16] Maya Patel: Ok we'll include a co-funded pilot option in the packet.

[10:22] Lucas Nguyen: Quick note for the benchmark: if you can provide a synthetic prompt set and a small customer prompt set, that'll help isolate latency vs quality tradeoffs.

[10:31] Ravi Singh: We'll pull together a 50-prompt pilot set and a 500-synthetic-workload.

[10:36] Samira Lopez: Also, can Redwood support compressed model variants like 4-bit quantization with per-layer scaling? Some of our customers want aggressive quantization.

[10:47] Lucas Nguyen: We support multiple quantization profiles including 4-bit QAT/LLM.int8-like flows; quality monitoring becomes more critical at that precision and we'll show expected deltas.

[10:58] Olivia Hart: Anyone on the call worried about data leaving the rack? Customers ask: where does telemetry go?

[11:05] Maya Patel: Telemetry can be configured to be hosted in your control plane only; we only request the minimal telemetry needed for observability. We'll also include a data flow diagram.

[11:15] Ravi Singh: Next — legal/contracting questions have come up about indemnity and data processing agreements. We'll expect a standard DPA and partner addendum.

[11:25] Maya Patel: Standard — we have a DPA and a partner addendum template. I'll loop legal on the thread once we agree on pilot scope.

[11:33] Olivia Hart: Great. Timeline recap? We want a benchmark next week, technical deep-dive the following week, commercial packet and pilot pricing by 2026-04-14, and pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-20.

[11:46] Maya Patel: That timeline works for us. Lucas, you good to run the benchmark and lead the deep-dive?

[11:54] Lucas Nguyen: Yes. I'll coordinate with Ravi on access and logistics.

[12:00] Samira Lopez: Quick question about observability: can tokens and cost be broken down per customer and per-route? Our sales team wants to show cost per feature.

[12:09] Lucas Nguyen: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-token cost breakdown, per-route latency, and per-model traces. We'll show a demo during the tech deep-dive.

[12:20] Olivia Hart: Any concerns about resale margins and EULA constraints? We don't want to be limited by host provider terms.

[12:28] Maya Patel: Our partner agreement allows resale and embedding; we have carve-outs for resellers and OEMs. We'll include the commercial model options.

[12:36] Ravi Singh: Technical follow-up — for the benchmark I'd like to test fallback policies under induced load. Can Redwood simulate node degradation?

[12:44] Lucas Nguyen: Yes, we have fault-injection for nodes and we can run degraded-load scenarios to show autoscaling, fallback models, and admission control.

[12:55] Maya Patel: Sounds like we're aligned. Final check: what else do you need from us to make the benchmark smooth?

[13:04] Ravi Singh: Access SOP, sample prompts, registry credentials (read-only), and a small test rack with jump host.

[13:12] Lucas Nguyen: I'll send a checklist and a Docker image for the runtime; if your infra team wants a pre-validated image we can provide an image SHA.

[13:22] Olivia Hart: For the contract side, we'll expect to review the partner addendum and the DPA. Samira will be the legal contact.

[13:30] Samira Lopez: Noted. We'll review and flag any changes.

[13:36] Maya Patel: Great. Any other questions?

[13:40] Olivia Hart: One last thing — can Redwood provide a short co-branded blurb for marketing if pilot goes well?

[13:47] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We can draft a short co-marketing one-pager.

[13:52] Lucas Nguyen: Ok I'll sync with Ravi on the benchmark window.

[13:56] Maya Patel: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security pack, checklist, and commercial starter packet.

[14:05] Olivia Hart: Thank you, looking forward to the next steps.

[14:10] (Call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-heard words in audio transcription — e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash' and 'SAML' as 'sam-el' in the automated notes. The meeting included a clear AE + SE pairing from Redwood and covered both commercial and deep technical items.

References shared during call: - Redwood partner starter packet (deck) — link to be sent - SOC 2 + network diagram — to be shared by Redwood - Benchmark checklist and runtime docker image (Lucas) — link to be sent

Footer: End of Fireflies export.
